subject: Computer Networking
title: Uninterruptible Power Supplies
description: Learn Uninterruptible Power Supplies in one minute.

hook.text: Power blinks for half a second. Your PC reboots, but a data center server keeps running. Thank the UPS.

buildup.text: A UPS provides battery backup the instant mains power fails. The switchover is instantaneous.

discovery.text: UPS units also clean incoming power: filtering spikes, sags, and noise that damage electronics.

twist.text: A UPS doesn't run servers for hours. It bridges 5-30 minutes until diesel generators take over.

climax.text: Data centers use room-sized UPS with thousands of batteries. Some use spinning flywheels instead.

punchline.text: A UPS buys time when power dies. Seconds matter in a data center.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a UPS in a data center?
options: Bridge the gap between power loss and generator startup
Cool the servers during high load

details.summary: An uninterruptible power supply provides battery backup that keeps network equipment running during power outages and protects against surges, sags, and electrical noise. UPS units give servers and switches enough time to shut down gracefully or ride through brief power interruptions.
details.whyItMatters: Power outages cause data loss, corruption, and hardware damage. A UPS provides critical minutes of runtime that prevent ungraceful shutdowns and protect sensitive network equipment.
takeaways: UPS batteries provide backup power during outages instantly
Line-interactive UPS units regulate voltage without switching to battery
Runtime depends on battery capacity and connected equipment load

faq.question: What types of UPS exist?
faq.answer: Standby UPS units switch to battery when power fails, with a brief transfer time. Line-interactive models regulate voltage continuously and switch to battery faster. Online double-conversion UPS units always run from battery, providing the cleanest power with zero transfer time.

faq.question: How long will a UPS keep equipment running?
faq.answer: Runtime depends on battery capacity and load. A typical 1500VA UPS powers a small network switch and server for 10 to 20 minutes. That is enough time for automated graceful shutdown. Larger rack-mounted UPS units with extended battery packs can provide hours of runtime.
